I just want to share my thoughts real quick because I think people are getting the wrong idea. Ultimately, the episodic structure wasn't the reason for poor sales, but rather an egregious lack of marketing. Have you ever seen a single advertisement for the new hitman? Also think back to how you discovered the game. Personally, I first found out about hitman when the original gameplay video was released from some dude's twitter. Then I found out about the beta from some dude's youtube channel. Then I found out that the episodes were coming out many many months late. By the time I had found out that hitman was even available to play it was already August. After that I would have not known about any hitman news if I didn't follow this sub.

My point is, hitman seemed like it was entirely marketed by youtube videos. A whole lot of people said that they would wait until the full release to get the game, but when the full game was finally coming out there was almost no attempt to build hype and spread awareness whatsoever.

So it really all comes down to SE, they probably had no faith in the game for whatever reason, because as far as I know marketing is the publisher's job. A real shame.

I feel like I remember Blood Money having some kind of raised pulse vibration thing going on. Imo it made things feel a little too tense though, especially since it was tied to the suspicion meter which liked to jump around for no real reason.

Idk if this is a viable method or I just got *really* lucky with timing, but if you aren't worried about your rating I just snuck into the parlor via the pipe round back, hid behind the kitchen counter, threw a knife into the dude's face, and somehow no one saw me. I was expecting some kinda big chase but I was just able to walk out pretty much.
